articles.title: Did Bell–Cisco Sovereign AI Pact Just Recast Cisco Systems' (CSCO) Regulated-Market Strategy?
articles.summary: In late September 2026, Bell Canada and Cisco announced a memorandum of understanding to build a sovereign AI infrastructure platform in Canada, combining Bell’s domestic data centres and networks with Cisco’s AI, security, observability, and Sovereign Critical Infrastructure technologies for customers with strict data residency and control needs. This move highlights how Cisco is trying to embed its AI-focused networking, security, and infrastructure stack into regulated markets where...

articles.title: The One Number Cisco Stock Investors Should Watch
articles.summary: You probably think of Cisco Systems (CSCO) as an AI stock, a supplier of AI infrastructure to the hyperscalers. That business was only about 6% of Cisco's revenue in fiscal 2026. The rest includes networking and security products sold to enterprises and telcos. Cisco stock returned 61% over the past year. With AI that small a share of revenue, you are paying for growth across the whole company. How fast is Cisco's business outside AI set to grow.

articles.title: The Dividend Stock I’m Adding Before October
articles.summary: A pullback just handed income investors a lower entry price than Cisco paid for its own shares, and the October record date is closing fast. Here is why this AI networking play keeps beating consumer staples for a dividend portfolio built around a rising quarterly check.

articles.title: What Could Surprise Cisco Stock Investors On The Upside?
articles.summary: Cisco Systems (CSCO) stock returned 62% over the past 12 months (as of Ssptember 28, 2026). After that run, you pay 31.8 times its past year's earnings, against 22.1 for the S&P 500. At that price, the stock appears to assume growth that has not happened yet, so further upside would need something beyond that. So what could still surprise Cisco Systems investors on the upside.
